A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dinitropyrenes are potent frameshift mutagens in E. coli that are capable of inducing a wide variety of base substitutions.

the mutational specificity associated with the dinitropyrenes is primarily dependent on the nature and location of the lesion in DNA, with a secondary influence from the cellular repair and tolerance mechanisms that are available.
1,6- and 1,8-NPONP are potent frameshift mutagens in E. coli that induce mutations at a high frequency at guanine residues, particularly those in runs of guanines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
1,6- and 1,8-Nitroso-nitropyrenes (NONPs) are highly efficient inducers of frameshift mutations, and that the mutational spectrum is strongly modulated by cellular repair or tolerance mechanisms.
the mutational specificity is highly influenced by the ability of a cell to remove DNA lesions and to carry out translesion synthesis.
